theory: Official account: overloaded legacy telecom switches and routers
label: Confirmed
gist: Duffy said on the record at the White House briefing (Reuters, BBC, LA Times, Aviation Week) that legacy analog TDM (time-division multiplexing) switches and routers carrying ATC voice and radar data were overloaded with data, began giving inconsistent data at 3:36 PM ET, and the FAA shut the system down; radar and communications were never fully lost. Mullin said new equipment being added was overwhelming the older system. This confirms what officials said, not an independent finding; no written FAA report, transcript, vendor or specific upgrade has been named.

theory: Saturday: Duffy names L3Harris copper-to-fiber work at a remote FAA site
label: Confirmed
gist: At the 10:30 AM ET Saturday DOT briefing with FAA Administrator Bedford, Duffy said the outage began while L3Harris Technologies, which runs the network, was switching lines from copper wire to fiber at a remote FAA site, and a router involved in that work flooded the rest of the system, disrupting communications with aircraft and radar (Yahoo News live coverage; AInvest wire headline). This confirms what Duffy said, not a finding: officials have not determined whether the router was faulty or the contractor erred ("Was it the router, or were they not doing great work for us at L3Harris?"). The site was not named, no written FAA report is posted, and L3Harris had not commented. The CBS software-update/reboot account stays Reported.

label: Reported
gist: Bloomberg, at 5:01 PM ET, citing one unnamed person familiar with the matter: the FBI is looking at whether a software update caused the outage and does not believe it was a cyberattack or crime. No vendor or product is named. The FBI has not commented. No independent corroboration was found; later mentions are re-reports of Bloomberg. Compatible with the CBS account but a separate claim.

label: Reported
gist: CBS, citing multiple unnamed sources: an update to the L3Harris-run ATC network caused a reboot and crash. Not officially confirmed. Officials now blame overloaded legacy switches and routers, and Mullin said new equipment overwhelmed the old system, which is compatible with an upgrade trigger but does not confirm an update, a reboot or L3Harris. Reuters separately reports, citing two airline officials, that the affected network is the L3Harris-overseen one.

label: Unverified
gist: CNN, as relayed by Fox 5 Vegas: the FAA told airlines the problem began with network routers, possibly at Chicago Midway. The FAA has not confirmed this publicly. Unconfirmed, and separate from the CBS and Bloomberg update accounts.

label: Unverified
gist: Mullin said on the record that CISA is "looking at" a possible link to SMART (GeekWire); that he said this is confirmed. Any actual SMART role remains unconfirmed. Vendor Air Space Intelligence denied that SMART caused the outage (on the record, via GeekWire). Later, per Reuters, Mullin said there is "zero evidence" so far of a rogue AI system, though it is not ruled out. AvWeb quotes Duffy saying SMART is not connected to the FAA's STARS or ERAM systems and that "There's no possible way SMART would have impacted what happened." AeroTime also reports that Duffy said SMART played no role. This stays Unverified because Reuters has Mullin saying a rogue AI is not fully ruled out.

label: Unverified
gist: Mullin said there is "zero evidence" so far of a cyberattack or a rogue AI system and that it "appears this was mechanically driven," but investigators have not ruled it out; the NSA is working with DHS (Reuters). Duffy said there was no evidence of a cyberattack or foreign involvement (LA Times).

label: Unverified
gist: Nothing public ties a fiber cut to today. The September cut near New Brunswick, N.J. is a prior event.

label: Unverified
gist: The 70% upgraded figure is confirmed. Officials blame old TDM copper switches and routers overwhelmed as new equipment was added, which fits a modernization-related trigger, but no cutover, vendor or date has been named, so a cutover as the cause stays unverified.

label: Rumor
gist: Partly true at most: AT&T won the FENS contract in August 2026, but only a $74.3M planning task is funded; L3Harris still operates FTI. Nothing public links AT&T to today's outage.

label: Rumor
gist: Unconfirmed. No official confirmation of a nationwide outage. Downdetector logged unverified user reports from 4:13 PM ET; Lincoln, NE and Tulare, CA lost only non-emergency lines.

label: Confirmed
gist: Canadian systems not hit, per NAV CANADA; only US-bound and some US-overflight flights stopped.

label: Debunked
gist: Debunked as a nationwide NWS/NEXRAD or radar.weather.gov outage. NWS said there is no radar outage, that radar.weather.gov is working, and that outdated isolated webpages caused the confusion; the circulating notice was stale Los Angeles office page text, archived as early as December 2025. NCEP said at 6:01 PM ET Friday that radar and network communications were normal, and NWS Birmingham and Huntsville said NEXRAD dataflow was nominal. Narrower and confirmed: a few airport terminal Doppler weather radars had brief Friday dropouts (Newark 12:19–12:44 PM ET, Milwaukee 12:46–3:53 PM ET), and when Boston's airport weather-radar feed was restored at 3:46 PM ET, NWS Boston noted that Boston Center had reported telecom issues — the FAA problem touching one feed, not a national Weather Service outage.

theory: Equipment already over capacity; L3Harris asked to diagnose
label: Reported
gist: A Saturday Hindustan Times explainer, citing Bloomberg and people familiar with an FAA industry briefing, says some of the equipment was already running over capacity and that once it was overwhelmed the failure spread to the old telecom backbone; it also says L3Harris has been asked to diagnose the overload. Those two Bloomberg details could not be independently confirmed in a Bloomberg text story, L3Harris has not commented, and the FAA has not confirmed them. Keep this Reported/unconfirmed, separate from the officials' on-record overload account.
